families.rationale: The rich-text finalization is sound. This family now emits canonical, boundary and negative fixtures and a contact sheet where it previously produced nothing; both pages of the source are preserved; the participant values are visible; and the sanitizer is thorough — the source's 100 /JS, 100 /JavaScript and 52 /AA entries and all 96 widgets are gone, /Annots is an empty array on both pages, and no /RV packet appears in the original bytes, in the decompressed streams or after re-saving with object streams off. The corpus audit records both rich-text fields as carrying no /RV packet, so no stale appearance could be flattened in, and the values on the page are the freshly written ones. The source binary is unmodified. What fails is a binding: the petitioner's name is written into the form's 'Other (include name and address of agency)' field. Because this family had never produced an artifact, no reviewer had ever been able to see it.

'County Where Arrest Occurred' is blank in the canonical and boundary bytes at its own widget rectangle [39.79, 502.6, 309.74, 516.21] on page 1; the glyphs the extractor returns there are present at the same position in the untouched source, so they are the printed label, not a written value. The field is absent from populated-fields.json. The seven fields that should carry values still do. One canonical run spans two overlapping source widget rectangles ('Case number' and 'Court ORI number'); those two rectangles overlap in the source itself and the run sits wholly inside 'Case number'.

NameAtty, StAddrAtty, MailAddrAtty, CityAtty, StateAtty and ZipCodeAtty are blank in both fixtures at their own rectangles on page 1; the fragments the extractor returns ('y', 'p') are drawn by the untouched source at the same coordinates. Five canonical runs overlap more than one source widget rectangle; NamePetitioner, StreetAddr, MailAddr, City, State and ZipCode are nested address boxes in the source, and every run sits wholly inside one of them.

The six runs that reopened this approval ('Clear Form', 'Lock & Save Form', 'Top of Page', 'Top of 1st Page') are absent from all three fixtures and from the rebuilt contact sheet. Three pages in, three out. The contact-sheet proof names the current canonical sha256. findings.visibleDefect: The profile records 172 lines read, 0 unreadable, 0 anchors and 0 candidate labels, which reads as 'the form was read and has no participant label'. It cannot mean that here: every one of this document's 10,503 text runs is a single character, so the run-level label matcher, which skips any run shorter than three characters, can never match anything. The line-level matcher needs a whole line to equal a label, and the caption draws 'Defendant' and 'DOB' on one shared baseline and 'No.' on another. The decoded caption does contain labels in the lane's own CAPTION_FACTS vocabulary; the count is a property of the matcher's granularity, and the profile does not say so.
findings.acceptanceCondition: Either the matcher can see labels below whole-line granularity on documents drawn one glyph per show operation, or the profile records that run granularity prevented matching, so 'overlay_no_participant_label_matched' cannot be read as a finding about the form.
findings.evidenceBasis: Run-length distribution measured from groupIntoLines on the verified source (10,503 runs, all length 1); the caption lines dumped with their runs; my replay of the lane's own OVERLAY_LABEL_BINDINGS, BLANK_BINDINGS and CAPTION_FACTS over the decoded text, which reproduces 0 matches.

families.rationale: The decoder fix is verified and it is good work. Where the old decoder read this Identity-H text layer as 21,122 meaningless byte-wide glyphs, the new one reads the form's real text: I decoded the same binary with MuPDF, an unrelated engine, and it confirms every line, and glyph positions agree to within 0.005pt across 8,764 characters. Nothing is misplaced because nothing is placed: this family has no fixtures, no contact sheet and an empty artifacts map. What I cannot sign off is the evidence the disposition rests on. And a zero candidate-label count that is forced by the matcher's granularity should not be recorded in a way that reads as a finding about the form. The existing source, legal and visual-review holds on this family are untouched by this review.

findings.visibleDefect: The profile reports unreadableLines 0 on every page, but the decoder's own gate (partitionDecodableAnchors) refuses 2 of this form's 197 lines with reason 'line_carries_undecoded_character_codes'. The renderer that wrote this profile does not use that gate: d2a-regenerate.mjs still filters readable lines with CID_ENCODED = /\u0000/, and the D0-v3 decoder marks an undecoded code with U+FFFD, not NUL, so no line can ever match. Lines the decoder itself cannot read are counted as readable and offered to the anchor matcher.
findings.acceptanceCondition: d2a-regenerate.mjs partitions lines with partitionDecodableAnchors and reports its refusal counts, so unreadableLines equals what the decoder actually refused and no undecodable line can become an anchor.

factoryLevelObservations.scope: shared factory, outside the 20 families' dispositions
factoryLevelObservations.observation: On forms drawn with simple TrueType fonts the decoder's per-character advances do not match the widths the fonts declare, and the error accumulates. On WA CRRLJ-09.0870 page 2 I compared one full-width line of 86 characters three ways: the font's own /Widths array (YASEES+ArialMT, FirstChar 32) gives 'v' and 'c' 500 units and 'o' and 'n' 556; MuPDF's rendered glyph origins agree exactly; the decoder advances roughly 0.58pt further per character for most glyphs. Both runs start at x=72.01 and the decoder's last glyph sits 37.36pt - about half an inch - to the right of where MuPDF puts it. On CRRLJ-09.0100 the worst line diverges by 24.46pt.
factoryLevelObservations.notARegression: The pre-D0-v3 decoder produces the identical 37.36pt divergence on the identical line, so this predates the anchor-decoder fix and was not introduced by it. On the Type0/Identity-H forms the fix targeted, the new decoder agrees with MuPDF to within 0.005pt across 17,914 characters.
factoryLevelObservations.whyItMattersAnyway: No anchor is derived from these four Washington forms, so nothing is misplaced on them. But the same decoder measures anchors for families that do write values from a label's position, and an anchor measured from a simple-font label can sit a column away from where it looks.
factoryLevelObservations.acceptanceCondition: The decoder's advance for a simple-font glyph equals the width the font declares for that code, checked against an independent engine on a form drawn with subset TrueType fonts.
factoryLevelObservations.evidenceBasis: per-character comparison of the decoder's own chars[] output against MuPDF glyph origins and against the /Widths array read from the font dictionary at xref 99 of the verified CRRLJ-09.0870 binary; the same comparison run with the decoder taken from claude/rcap-d2a-approval-evidence-v2.

toolsUsed: MuPDF 1.28.2 via PyMuPDF, as an engine unrelated to the factory's pdf-lib path
the factory's own rcap-pdf-anchor-capture.mjs and d0-v3-corpus-decode-audit.mjs, run from a copy outside every git worktree
raw byte scans of the original files, of every FlateDecode stream decompressed, and of each file re-saved with object streams off and streams expanded

determinism.whatIVerified: for each of the 16 families that produce artifacts, the recorded determinism evidence names two renders with the same sha256 and that sha256 is the hash of the canonical fixture actually on the branch; creation and modification dates are pinned to D:20260101000000Z in every artifact I opened
determinism.whatIDidNotDo: I did not render anything a second time myself. The assignment forbids re-rendering, and the lane scripts write into the family directories they would have to be run against. So determinism is verified as recorded-and-tied-to-the-bytes, not as independently reproduced.
determinism.washingtonNote: the four Washington families record rendered: false with the reason that no finalized artifact was produced, which matches the empty artifacts map and the absent fixtures

methodAndLimits.boundaryFixtureNote: Boundary fixtures carry deliberately long values that differ from the canonical ones, so a canonical value missing from a boundary fixture is expected and is not treated as a defect.
methodAndLimits.controlCaptionRule: A run inside a non-printing widget's rectangle was called a leak only when it also belonged to no overlapping printing widget and did not appear in the untouched source's own page content at that position. Contact sheets compose two scaled panels, so source widget rectangles do not apply to them; they were judged by panel attribution instead.
methodAndLimits.notReviewed: the other 233 D-wave families; no implementation, correction or evidence branch was modified; no legal or source hold was reopened; nothing here approves a family for live use or marks any track terminal
